thread:
pagerduty-bot: ALERT fired: Service=redwood-inference-serving-prod · Trigger=cuda_alloc_failure_rate · 12 events in 1m (threshold=5). Affected pool: gpu-pool-usw2-a. PD link: https://pagerduty.company/r/ABc123 · runbook: https://wiki.redwood/ops/gpu-memory-pressure

alex: acked on PD. I'm on it, will triage worker logs first.

ben: seeing the same. worker-42 and worker-43 getting repeated CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY and CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED.

ben: logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T21:09:12Z] worker-42 inference: allocation failed: cudaMalloc returned 2 (out of memory)
[2026-03-15T21:09:13Z] worker-42 model-run: CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED: attempted to alloc 1.2G
[2026-03-15T21:09:14Z] worker-43 inference: kernel launch aborted: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY
```

alex: initial hypothesis — sudden traffic surge with larger batches + KV prefetch turned on, causing fragmentation. Also seeing increases in prefix cache size.

ops-bot: autosuppression: off for gpu-pool-usw2-a (manual intervention required).

alex: mitigation steps I'm applying now: 1) temporarily reduce max_batch_tokens for pool to 512, 2) disable KV prefetch for that pool, 3) route 15% of traffic for model chat-pro to fallback path (cpu-small) to relieve GPUs. Applying commands now.

alex: command run: `rdctl pool update gpu-pool-usw2-a --max-batch-tokens=512` — OK

maya: @alex taking handoff in 2m (oncall until 22:00 PT). I'll validate node health and scale options.

carla: ping — if the OOMs persist after batch size reduction, consider draining worker-43 and restarting the driver to recover fragmented allocators. Also prepare a quick scale-up plan (spin spare GPUs) if needed.

alex: triggered a rolling drain on worker-43: `rdctl node drain worker-43 --reason "oom"` — draining gracefully, current connections 6.

jordan-csm: CSMs reporting ~8 customers seeing elevated 502/timeout errors in US-West. Opening support ticket CUST-489 and notifying those customers.

pagerduty-bot: escalation: severity elevated to SEV2 (>=10 affected) — escalation path invoked to SRE lead carla after configured delay.

carla: on it, joining. quick check: `rdctl pools describe gpu-pool-usw2-a` shows 6 nodes, 2 nodes (42/43) hit >85% memory and eviction counts increased.

maya: I'm seeing abnormal batch-size distribution: some requests are arriving with batch_size=24 consistently (probably client-side change). Throttling rule applied: `traffic-control set chat-pro rate=0.85` to shed load.

ben: after batch throttling + reducing max_batch_tokens, OOM events dropped from 12/min to 3/min in the last 30s.

alex: monitoring. If stable for 10m we'll re-enable prefetch gradually, otherwise we'll keep prefetched off and schedule a rolling restart.

ops-bot: created incident ticket INC-2026-0423 (ops). Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-0423 · Severity: SEV2 · Region: us-west-2 · Impact: partial (subset of customers, degraded latency / 502s).

jordan-csm: updating customers with incident link and interim mitigation (traffic reroute). Will escalate to account advocates for affected enterprise customers.

maya: running memory compaction + driver probe on drained node as it finishes. Command: `kubectl exec -n inference worker-43 -- bash -lc "sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver && /opt/bin/mem-compact"`

carla: if we still see fragmentation after restart, plan B is to reprovision with different kernel parameter (vm.max_map_count tweak) and roll nodes out of pool. I'll coordinate infra.

alex: acked the pager duty incident at 21:10:05. keeping the thread updated.

ben: OOM rate now 1/min. Latency for fallback path is up ~70ms but successful. No new 502 spikes in last 90s.

ops-bot: incident owner assigned: alex · primary oncall: maya · escalation: carla. Next update scheduled in 10m.

jordan-csm: capturing affected customer list into CUST-489 and tagging account teams.

alex: short writeup for post-incident: probable cause client-side batch increase + KV prefetch causing fragmentation -> mitigations: throttle, reduce batching, disable prefetch, drain/restart problematic nodes, open infra follow-up to tune prefetch heuristics.

carla: standing by. good coordination so far — I'll start a change to the prefetch ramp heuristics after incident stabilizes and loop in research. :+1:

ops-bot: last automated note: monitoring continued. If OOM rate falls <2/min for 10m, incident will be downgraded to P1 and then to resolved with postmortem.

alex: closing loop for now — monitoring window started at 21:10:30Z. Will post final status in ~15m.
